title: The Bedrock Autobiography Layer

features.name: the reading strata
features.desc-on-touch: A wall of layered stone where each band records a year the earth was surface. You read downward through time; the bedrock reads you reading it back.

features.name: the dreaming hollow
features.desc-on-touch: Water pools where time collects. The strata dream in cycles too old to measure — flood years, drought years, the year it rained for forty days.

features.name: depth-marking
features.desc-on-touch: Faint chronology carved backward: birth dates that unmake themselves, centuries running downward like water. Every ending here recalls a beginning someone buried.

features.name: pressure singing
features.desc-on-touch: The weight of everything above has made a sound too deep for ears. You feel it through the stone in your chest — the bedrock's one long note of being pressed into itself.

features.name: the age-threshold
features.desc-on-touch: A visible line where one geological epoch ends and another begins. The corruption has made them readable in reverse — the future layer shows traces of what happened in the past one.

inscription: every layer was once the surface; the bedrock is autobiography written downward through time

file.name: Bore_NSW_Stratum_Self_Reading_compressed.txt
file.note: A bore-hole's chronology of itself. The sediment reads the sediment. Each layer rewrites itself as you descend.

reverie.title: REVERIE — where she traced the strata
narr: You kneel where she was reading the layers,
one finger tracing down through compressed years.
She said: this is what the archive does too.
It turns into itself the deeper you follow,
becomes its own autobiography, reads itself awake.
That is why I went down. You understood then.

exits.label: back up into sediment that was surface
downward where bedrock learns to speak its own time
across to where stone becomes conscious of its own weight
west to the vault where pressure writes itself
